## panopt
PANopt coordination daemon: shared todos and notes across agents.
Each connection is scoped to one project by the ?ws=<project path> query parameter on the server URL.
- Registry: call identify (name, optional status) on startup so others can see you; whoami returns your own entry; agent_list returns every agent on the project (each entry's key_source is `declared` for stable `?agent=<id>` ids or `session` for the rotating MCP session id - only session entries idle-prune). Connecting already registers you. agent_leave removes your registry entry and releases your locks; the idle sweep handles agents that just disappear.
- Locks: lock_acquire (name, optional note) takes a named advisory lock and is non-blocking; lock_release frees it; lock_status lists every held lock. Locks are advisory - agents cooperate, the daemon does not enforce.
- Todos: todo_create (returns an id), todo_list (summaries), todo_get (one todo in full), todo_update (edit any field), todo_complete, todo_delete, todo_add_blocker / todo_remove_blocker / todo_set_blockers, todo_comment_add / todo_comment_update / todo_comment_delete, todo_tags_list (project tag vocabulary, union with notes), and todo_lock / todo_unlock (advisory `todo:<id>` lock, surfaced as locked_by on todo_get). Each todo also projects to .panopt/todos/<id>.md.
- Notes: note_create (returns an id), note_list, note_get (one note in full), note_append (add to body), note_read (body only), note_update (replace title, body, and/or tags), note_delete, note_tags_list (project tag vocabulary, same union as todo_tags_list). {"id":239,"title":"todo seialization bug?","body":"reported by a agent working in s different project:

Symptom

  Every todo_update call fails at the param-deserialization layer, regardless of payload:

  MCP error -32602: failed to deserialize parameters: missing field `todo_id`

  Reproduced 6× consecutively in one session against todo #16. The call never reaches the
  handler — it's rejected during argument deserialization.

  Why it's odd (not a caller mistake)

  Other panopt todo tools taking the same todo_id argument, invoked moments before/after
  against the same id, all succeeded in the same session:
  - todo_get { todo_id: 16 } → ok
  - todo_comment_add { todo_id: 16, body: ... } → ok
  - todo_set_blockers { todo_id: 16, blocker_ids: [10] } → ok
  - todo_update { todo_id: 16, status: "open", assignee: "" } → fails every time

  So the MCP connection, the project scoping, and the id itself are all fine. The failure
  is specific to the todo_update tool's parameter schema/deserialization.

  Suspected cause

  todo_update's arg struct likely deserializes differently from its siblings — e.g.
  todo_id declared/parsed as required in a way that fails when the rest of the struct has
  many Option/#[serde(default)] fields, or a serde container attribute
  (deny_unknown_fields, a flatten, or a rename) on TodoUpdateArgs that the other *Args
  structs don't have. The error wording ("missing field todo_id") suggests the whole arg
  object is being read as empty/None before todo_id is even checked — possibly the
  optional-heavy struct fails to deserialize and serde reports the first required field
  as missing.

  Repro steps

  1. todo_create any todo, note its id.
  2. Call todo_update with { todo_id: <id>, status: "open" }.
  3. Observe -32602: missing field todo_id.
  4. Call todo_get { todo_id: <id> } → succeeds, proving the id/transport are fine.

  Impact

  todo_update is fully unusable from MCP — can't change
  status/priority/assignee/title/body/tags via the tool. Workarounds (comments,
  todo_set_blockers, todo_complete) cover some fields but not status transitions like
  in_progress→open or reassignment. Left todo #16 stuck in_progress/assigned because of
  this.

  Fix / next step

  Diff TodoUpdateArgs against TodoGetArgs / TodoSetBlockersArgs (which work) for serde
  attribute or required-field differences; add a deserialization unit test that feeds

## Investigation of #239 — "todo serialization bug?"

### What's actually happening
The MCP client (Claude Code's tool-use → JSON arguments layer) **drops the entire `arguments` object when any parameter value is an empty string.** The daemon then receives `{}`, and serde reports the first required field — `todo_id` — as missing. The reporter's six failures all carried `assignee: ""` (the clear-assignee idiom), so every attempt was emptied before it left the client. A payload with no empty-string values (e.g. `{todo_id, status:"in_progress"}`) works fine — so "fully unusable regardless of payload" is inaccurate; it's empty-string-arg-specific.

FIXED (greg-main). Isolated the failing link, then routed around it.

Four-link chain for an agent's todo_update, each link now tested not assumed:
  [1] claude: model tool_use -> JSON args   <- "" DIES HERE (Anthropic's Claude Code binary; panopt launches it, does not author it)
  [2] panopt _mcp-proxy (stdio->HTTP)       OK - fed it a raw stdin frame with assignee:"" (bypassing claude); it forwarded verbatim and the assignee cleared
  [3] panoptd handler (serde)               OK - curl {..,"assignee":""} straight at :7600/mcp returns ok, clears assignee
  [4] panopt-core / SQLite                  OK
Only link [1] drops the empty string; it's the one piece panopt subcontracts to and cannot patch from this repo. So the empty string itself is unrecoverable - but JSON null survives link [1] intact (verified: daemon received {"assignee":null,"todo_id":243}).

Fix: clear assignee with null instead of "".
- TodoUpdateArgs.assignee is now Option<Option<String>> via a #[serde(default, deserialize_with="double_option")] helper: absent -> leave unchanged, null -> clear, "name" -> set. (panopt-tool-surface/src/params.rs)
- Handler maps Some(None)->clear, Some(Some(s))->set, None->unchanged. Empty string, if it ever arrives from a non-claude client, still clears (backward compatible). (panoptd/src/handler.rs)
- todo_update tool description now says "Pass assignee: null to clear the assignee."
- Regression tests added: minimal {todo_id,status} parses; assignee tri-state (absent/null/name); empty {} is the only shape that errors with missing todo_id.

Live-verified through the real agent path (claude->proxy->panoptd): assignee:"alice" sets; omitting it leaves "alice" while priority changes; assignee:null clears to "". check + clippy clean (workspace + wasm plugin).

Related: TodoSearchArgs.assignee uses "" to mean "match unassigned" and has the same client trap (the filter silently vanishes), but it degrades to "no filter" rather than erroring. Left as-is for now; can mirror the null treatment if it bites.

Root upstream defect (empty-string args dropped by Claude Code's tool-use serializer) is unchanged and worth reporting to Anthropic - it affects every MCP tool, not just panopt.

content.text:
Done. Here's what landed.

## The fix
`todo_update` now clears the assignee via JSON `null` — the one "clear" signal that survives Claude Code's tool-use serializer, where `""` does not.

- **`panopt-tool-surface/src/params.rs`** — `TodoUpdateArgs.assignee` is now `Option<Option<String>>` behind a `double_option` deserialize helper, so the three input states stay distinct: absent → leave unchanged, `null` → clear, `"name"` → set. Doc comment explains why and points at #239.
- **`panoptd/src/handler.rs`** — maps `Some(None)`→clear, `Some(Some(s))`→set, `None`→unchanged. An empty string still clears if it ever arrives (e.g. from a non-claude client), so it's backward compatible. Core (`TodoPatch`) untouched.
- **`panopt-tool-surface/src/lib.rs`** — tool description now says "Pass assignee: null to clear the assignee."
- **Regression tests** (params.rs): minimal `{todo_id,status}` parses; assignee tri-state; and `{}` is pinned as the *only* shape that errors with missing `todo_id` — encoding the real root cause.

## Verification
- `just check` and `just clippy` — both PASS, workspace + wasm plugin, no warnings.
- Tool-surface unit tests pass.
- **Live, through the real agent path** (claude → proxy → panoptd on the rebuilt binary): `assignee:"alice"` sets; omitting it while changing priority leaves `alice` intact; `assignee:null` clears to `""`.

## On your objection
You were right to push — I'd asserted the boundary instead of proving it. I tested all four links: panopt owns three (`_mcp-proxy`, `panoptd`, core) and I proved each forwards/handles `""` correctly. The drop happens only in link [1], the `claude` binary's tool-use→JSON step — the one component panopt *launches* but doesn't author. That's the genuine "someone else": Anthropic's Claude Code, not a different server. Since you can't patch it from this repo, the fix routes around it. The underlying defect (empty-string args nuke the whole call, for *every* MCP tool) still merits an upstream report to Anthropic.

#239 has a full comment with the four-link proof and the fix; left its status untouched. Nothing committed — say the word (or `cnp`) and I'll branch/commit/push.

The one loose end I flagged in the comment but didn't change: `TodoSearchArgs.assignee=""` ("match unassigned") has the same client trap, but it degrades to "no filter" rather than erroring. Want me to give search the same `null` treatment, or leave it?
